module.title: Distributed Systems And Scalable Infrastructure
module.description: Learn how large-scale applications distribute workloads, synchronize systems, handle massive traffic, and build globally scalable infrastructure.

lessons.title: What Are Distributed Systems?

definition.title: Simple Definition
definition.content: Distributed systems are applications where multiple servers and services work together as one large system.

sections.heading: Single Servers Have Limits
sections.content: One machine cannot reliably handle millions of users, requests, and data operations alone.

sections.heading: Modern Applications Are Distributed
sections.content: Large systems spread workloads across many servers, regions, and services.

sections.heading: Distributed Infrastructure Improves Scalability
sections.content: Traffic, storage, processing, and communication distribute across multiple systems.

sections.heading: Professional Engineering Focus
sections.content: Modern backend engineering heavily relies on distributed architecture thinking.

easyExample.title: Chain Restaurant Example
easyExample.content: One restaurant can only serve limited customers, but restaurant chains distribute service across many locations.

basicCode.title: Distributed Infrastructure Example
basicCode.code:
Frontend Servers
API Servers
Database Cluster

summary: Single servers cannot handle huge scale
Scalable engineering relies on distributed architecture

definition.title: Simple Definition
definition.content: Distributed communication allows multiple services and servers to exchange information reliably.

sections.heading: Distributed Systems Must Coordinate
sections.content: Authentication, payments, notifications, analytics, and APIs constantly communicate together.

sections.heading: Service-to-Service Communication
sections.content: Applications exchange information through APIs, events, queues, and messaging systems.

sections.heading: Network Complexity
sections.content: Distributed communication creates latency, failures, and synchronization challenges.

sections.heading: Professional Infrastructure Design
sections.content: Large companies carefully design communication systems for reliability and scalability.

easyExample.title: Airport Communication Example
easyExample.content: Airports require coordination between security, baggage systems, pilots, and control towers.

basicCode.title: Service Request Example
basicCode.code: Auth Service → User Service → Notification Service

definition.title: Simple Definition
definition.content: Consistency ensures distributed systems maintain correct and synchronized data across servers.

sections.heading: Distributed Data Creates Complexity
sections.content: Multiple systems storing copies of data can become inconsistent.

sections.heading: Synchronization Problems
sections.content: Servers must update information correctly across distributed infrastructure.

sections.heading: Consistency Models
sections.content: Some systems prioritize perfect consistency while others prioritize speed and availability.

sections.heading: Production Engineering Tradeoffs
sections.content: Large companies carefully balance scalability, reliability, and consistency.

easyExample.title: Bank ATM Example
easyExample.content: All ATM machines must display updated account balances correctly across different locations.

lessons.title: Distributed Caching Systems

definition.title: Simple Definition
definition.content: Distributed caching stores data across multiple systems to improve scalability and performance.

sections.heading: Single Cache Servers Become Bottlenecks
sections.content: Large applications require distributed cache infrastructure for massive traffic.

sections.heading: Distributed Cache Clusters
sections.content: Caching systems spread data across multiple nodes.

sections.heading: Performance Optimization
sections.content: Distributed caching significantly reduces database pressure and improves speed.

sections.heading: Production Infrastructure Dependency
sections.content: Large companies heavily rely on distributed Redis clusters and caching systems.

easyExample.title: Warehouse Network Example
easyExample.content: Companies distribute products across warehouses globally for faster delivery.

summary: Large systems rely heavily on Redis clusters
Performance optimization depends on distributed caching

lessons.title: Pub/Sub And Messaging Systems

definition.title: Simple Definition
definition.content: Pub/Sub systems allow services to communicate through events and message broadcasting.

sections.heading: Direct Communication Creates Tight Coupling
sections.content: Directly connecting every service creates scalability and maintenance problems.

sections.heading: Publish Subscribe Architecture
sections.content: Services publish events while other services subscribe and react independently.

sections.heading: Distributed Event Systems
sections.content: Modern systems use Kafka, Redis Pub/Sub, and messaging queues heavily.

sections.heading: Scalable Distributed Workflows
sections.content: Event-driven communication improves scalability and flexibility.

easyExample.title: Radio Broadcast Example
easyExample.content: Radio stations broadcast signals while listeners subscribe independently.

summary: Modern infrastructure relies heavily on event broadcasting

lessons.title: Production Distributed Engineering Thinking

definition.title: Simple Definition
definition.content: Production distributed engineering focuses on scalable, fault-tolerant, globally distributed systems handling massive infrastructure workloads.

sections.heading: Modern Applications Are Distributed Ecosystems
sections.content: Frontend systems, APIs, databases, caches, queues, messaging systems, and cloud infrastructure all work together globally.

sections.heading: Distributed Engineering Is Complex
sections.content: Scalability introduces communication delays, synchronization problems, failures, and infrastructure coordination challenges.

sections.heading: Large Companies Depend On Distributed Systems
sections.content: Netflix, Google, Amazon, and Meta rely heavily on distributed architecture.

sections.heading: Thinking Beyond Single Servers
sections.content: Professional engineers think about infrastructure ecosystems instead of isolated applications.

easyExample.title: Global Shipping Network Example
easyExample.content: Global logistics companies coordinate warehouses, transportation, tracking, and delivery systems worldwide.

basicCode.title: Production Distributed Flow
basicCode.code: Users → CDN → Load Balancer → API Cluster → Queue → Worker Cluster → Database Replicas

summary: Large-scale systems rely heavily on distributed architecture
Professional engineering focuses on scalable ecosystems
